limits: For white wine, Sauvignon: at least 70%
For red wine, Pinot Noir: at least 10%
For red wine, Cot: at least 10%
For red wine, Cabernet Franc: at most 20%
For rosé wine, Pinot Noir: at least 10%
For rosé wine, Cot: at least 10%
For rosé wine, Cabernet Franc: at most 20%
For rosé wine, Pineau D'Aunis: at most 30%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white, 55 for red and rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

blurb.text: A Touraine appellation in the upper Loire, on the left bank of the Cher. It is the only place in France with an appellation for both wine and cheese. Sauvignon Blanc is the main white grape, and reds are made from Cot, Gamay and Pinot Noir.
